title: Bud Wilkinson's Three National Titles at Oklahoma: 1950, 1955, 1956
question: How many national championships did Bud Wilkinson win at Oklahoma?
answer: Three: 1950, 1955 and 1956. Wilkinson went 145-29-4 at Oklahoma from 1947 through 1963 and won 14 conference championships in 17 seasons.
summary: Bud Wilkinson led Oklahoma to national titles in 1950, 1955 and 1956 and went 145-29-4. A look at each championship team and the coach who built the dynasty.
body: Bud Wilkinson took over at Oklahoma in 1947 at age 31, and over the next 17 seasons he turned the Sooners into a national power. His teams went 145-29-4, won 14 conference championships and put together winning streaks of 31 and 47 games. Three of those teams finished as national champions.

The first came in 1950. Oklahoma went 10-0 in the regular season, and both major polls named the Sooners champions before the bowls, as was the custom then. Kentucky beat them 13-7 in the Sugar Bowl on Jan. 1, 1951, but that game came after the voting.

The 1955 team left no doubt. The Sooners went 11-0, outscored opponents 385-60 and finished No. 1 in both the AP and coaches polls. In the Orange Bowl on Jan. 2, 1956, they trailed Maryland 6-0 at halftime and then scored 20 unanswered points to win 20-6. Halfback Tommy McDonald led the team in scoring.

The 1956 Sooners may have been the best of the three. They went 10-0, averaged 46.6 points per game, allowed just 51 points all year and posted six shutouts, including 45-0 over Texas and 40-0 at Notre Dame. Center and co-captain Jerry Tubbs was an All-American and a Heisman finalist. The team didn't play in a bowl because the Big Seven's no-repeat rule kept it home.
Wilkinson was inducted into the College Football Hall of Fame in 1969. He was proud of the classroom too; close to 90 percent of his players earned degrees.
